name: Jonathan Iker Zamarripa
headline: A different way to see learning.
intro: Talks on cinematic learning, AI-era design, and the person on the other side of the experience.
bio: Jonathan Iker Zamarripa designs learning the way a director builds a scene. A learning experience designer and the founder of Cinematic Learning Systems, he created the Cinematic Learning Production Framework: an openly published framework for designing learning through cinematic grammar and AI. His work connects enterprise learning, leadership development, technology enablement, and creative production.
shortBio: Jonathan Iker Zamarripa is a learning experience designer and the founder of Cinematic Learning Systems. He created the Cinematic Learning Production Framework, an openly published framework for designing learning through cinematic grammar and AI, and writes about cinematic learning on LinkedIn.

publication.title: Cinematic Learning Production Framework
publication.note: A practitioner-theorist framework, not an empirically validated intervention.

talks.title: The Other Person in the Room
talks.teaser: What changes when we design the counterpart, not just the learner’s choices?
talks.description: Practice scenarios vary what the learner says. They rarely vary who the other person is. This talk explores designing the counterpart with a hidden state the learner has to read, and what that changes about a simulation’s learning possibilities.
talks.audience: Leadership development, learning design conferences, and keynote audiences
talks.takeaway: A way to examine counterpart design, readable cues, and the decisions a practice scenario asks learners to make.

talks.title: Measure the Film, Not the Dailies
talks.teaser: Separate performance with AI support from learning that lasts.
talks.description: AI can raise performance in a session without building skill that lasts. This talk examines a practical evaluation rule: without the support, after a delay, in a case the learner hasn’t seen.
talks.audience: L&D and AI enablement conferences, evaluation tracks, and learning teams
talks.takeaway: Questions for planning unsupported, delayed, and unfamiliar-case assessments alongside in-session measures.

talks.title: Telling Them It’s AI Isn’t Enough
talks.teaser: Design disclosure into the experience, not just its opening label.
talks.description: What does a learner need to understand before an AI-mediated scene, during it, and after? This talk explores disclosure as an experience-design decision, with attention to learner expectations, boundaries, and transparency.
talks.audience: Ethics panels, university courses, HR, compliance, and learning-design teams
talks.takeaway: A before, during, and after lens for examining how an AI experience explains itself to learners.
